source.title: Towards Quantifying Intrinsic Generalization of Deep ReLU Networks
source.authors: Shaeke Salman; Can-Lin Zhang; Xiu-Wen Liu; W. Mio

record.tranche_reason: The study trains ReLU networks on real and randomized labels and reports training error and validation accuracy, while its main measure is generalization intervals rather than the original studies’ fit-and-test evaluation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports near-zero training error and validation accuracy for MNIST with real and randomized labels. Its generalization-interval findings are recorded as results about the claim’s subject, but those intervals do not measure the outcomes named by V1–V6. Citations to Zhang et al. and Arpit et al. are not counted as this study’s results.
record.test_reason: Section 4.1 reports the study's own SGD training on fully randomized MNIST labels, near-zero training error, and chance-level held-out accuracy. These directly measure V1 using the original type of training-and-evaluation method, although the paper mainly studies interpolation intervals.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: deep ReLU networks interpolate around training samples, with similar pairwise intervals under real and random labels in high dimensions, while real-label interpolations approximate underlying manifolds. Their distinction between interpolation and literal point-only memorization does not contradict the operational random-label fitting claim in V1.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SGD with learning rate 0.01 and ReLU networks trained on real or randomized labels, but measures generalization intervals rather than reproducing the original studies’ full training-time and test-error analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: Input dimension changes the interval distributions: lower-dimensional MNIST shows lower intervals for random labels; the two-dimensional two moons result shows a dramatic distribution change after randomizing labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Pairwise interpolation intervals are similar for real and randomized labels in high-dimensional MNIST and CIFAR-10; random-label intervals become smaller with reduced dimension and along triangle midlines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Similarity of classification stability under real and random labels depends on input dimension and measurement direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Pairwise interval distributions remain roughly similar across tested network depths.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested MNIST architectures have similar pairwise interpolation-interval distributions.

fits_no_version.finding: Average interpolation intervals correlate with validation accuracy during training on actual MNIST labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Average interpolation intervals track held-out performance during true-label training in the tested MNIST setup.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Network
record.problems: The paper gives qualitative descriptions rather than numerical summaries for the generalization-interval distributions shown in figures. The stated MNIST training error is only 'very close to 0'; exact values and uncertainty are not reported. The reported validation accuracy is not test accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Generalization-interval results are retained because they are the study’s own measurements about interpolation on real and random labels; the separate panels without a textual result are marked figure only.

untested.parts: Explicit verification that architecture and all training hyperparameters remain unchanged between real-label and random-label runs; separate fitting and held-out results for each architecture and dataset.
Relative training time and convergence as label corruption increases.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training fit and held-out error across intermediate label-corruption fractions.
Effects of adding or removing weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels are memorized.

record.verdict_notes: Held-out validation accuracy supplies the relevant chance-performance evidence; its designation as validation rather than test accuracy is not itself a contrary result. The study's interpolation findings do not test V6 merely because real and random labels exhibit different spatial behavior.

versions.untested_parts: The text reports MNIST validation accuracy, not test error; it does not report training time or verify every architecture’s fit and validation results.
